# Incident Report — Traffic Analysis Exercise 2022-01-07

**Evidence:** `2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,880 packets, SHA256 `a86b11ee443ee59d95e4590bdf761235c5d240128d6d195233d065ab57777e8b`). No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence folder; all findings below are derived directly from the pcap with tshark.

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 192.168.1.216 |
| MAC address | 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9 (ASUS NIC vendor) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (confirmed via DHCP option 12 and mDNS/LLMNR self-queries) |
| Logged-in domain user | steve.smith (observed as Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString on the `spoonwatch.net` Active Directory domain, DC = SPOONWATCH-DC / 192.168.1.2) |
| LAN | 192.168.1.0/24, gateway 192.168.1.1, DC 192.168.1.2 |

## Malware family

**Vidar Stealer** (Arkei/Predator-the-Thief lineage). Attribution is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed** — no Suricata/IDS alert file was provided, and identification here rests on traffic-pattern and payload analysis:

- HTTP client fingerprint is an exact match for Vidar's Indy/Delphi HTTP stack: no `User-Agent` header, and the header set `Accept: text/html, application/xml;q=0.9, application/xhtml+xml, image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/x-xbitmap, */*;q=0.1` / `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8` / `Accept-Charset: iso-8859-1, utf-8, utf-16, *;q=0.1` / `Accept-Encoding: deflate, gzip, x-gzip, identity, *;q=0`.
- The malware `GET`s a config/panel path at `/osk/`, then downloads 7 files named `1.jpg` through `7.jpg` from the C2 — each response is actually a Windows PE32 DLL (MZ header) served with `Content-Type: image/jpeg`. Extracted `strings` from these "jpg" files show legitimate but attacker-supplied support libraries: `sqlite3.dll`, `freebl3.dll`, `nss3.dll`, `softokn3.dll`, `nssdbm3.dll`, `mozglue`/`msvcp140.dll`/`vcruntime140.dll` components — the exact helper-DLL set Vidar fetches to parse SQLite/NSS browser credential stores.
- The malware then `POST`s a 379,629-byte multipart body to `/osk/` containing a file named `_5861695120.zip`. Carving that ZIP out of the capture shows the classic Vidar stealer-log structure: `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`, `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `system.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` (plain HTTP, no TLS, no DNS lookup — the malware connects to this IP directly with no domain resolution). Server banner: `Apache/2.4.12 (Win32) OpenSSL/1.0.1m PHP/5.3.29 mod_wsgi/4.4.11 Python/2.7.10`. First contact: 2022-01-07 20:07:32 (capture-local time), source port 49738.

**Malicious domains:** none — the malware communicates with the C2 by raw IP address only; no C2-related DNS query appears in the capture.

**Malicious URLs (all to 2.56.57.108)**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (POST — panel check-in and final data exfiltration, 379,629-byte multipart upload)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` (POST — 25-byte beacon)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `http://2.56.57.108/osk//7.jpg` (POST requests of 25 bytes each; each response delivers a payload DLL disguised as a jpg)

**Transferred files / hashes**

| File (as served) | Real type | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| `1.jpg` | PE32 DLL (console) | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` |
| `2.jpg` | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` |
| `3.jpg` | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` |
| `4.jpg` | PE32 DLL (console) | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` |
| `5.jpg` | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` |
| `6.jpg` | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083` |
| `7.jpg` | PE32 DLL (console) | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` |
| `_5861695120.zip` (uploaded, stolen-data exfil archive) | ZIP | `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f` (SHA256 of the raw upload body carrying it; the ZIP's own object hash was not separately computed, contents listed above) |

**Note on incidental noise:** the capture also shows ordinary Windows Update / Delivery Optimization / MSN / Bing / WNS traffic to Microsoft infrastructure (`23.38.189.225`, `23.38.189.201`, `52.249.36.204`, `52.178.17.2`, `204.79.197.200/203`, `40.83.240.146`, `184.50.62.43`, `20.x.x.x` ranges, `8.253.189.126`) and normal AD/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB traffic to the domain controller `SPOONWATCH-DC` (192.168.1.2). None of this is malicious; it is included in the conversation stats only as background and should not be flagged as IOC.

## Summary

DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), logged in as domain user `steve.smith` on the `spoonwatch.net` AD domain, was infected with a Vidar-family information stealer. The malware retrieved browser-parsing support DLLs disguised as JPEGs from C2 `2.56.57.108:80`, harvested Chrome/Edge autofill data, cookies, saved passwords, Outlook data, a screenshot, and system information, packaged it as `_5861695120.zip`, and exfiltrated it back to the same C2 over plain HTTP.
